question.text: A proton is moving with a uniform velocity of $10^{6} \mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ along the $Y$ -axis, under the joint action of a magnetic field along $Z$ -axis and an electric field of magnitude $2 \times 10^{4} \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$ along the negative $X$ -axis. If the electric field is switched off, the proton starts moving in a circle. The radius of the circle is nearly given: $\frac{e}{m}$ ratio for proton $=10^{4} \mathrm{Ckg}^{-1}$
